_note: Retention class per advisor seat, for the send preview (thc-research brief 29, seeded from brief 31's retention-classes-2026-09-30.json, which used fetched/brief-25/01, 02, 04, 08). A DATED SNAPSHOT of OpenRouter's public endpoint list and each lab's own terms: it goes stale. Re-check the ZDR tags (openrouter.ai/api/v1/endpoints/zdr) and the lab pages before relying on a row, and move `asOf` only when every row was re-checked. A ZDR tag is OpenRouter's statement about its own account with the host; for Azure and Vertex it is not a property of the cloud. Nothing here claims data is protected, and no live request has ever been made to see what OpenRouter does with provider.zdr.

classes.A: zero-retention-tagged endpoint by OpenRouter, at least one tagged EU
classes.B: zero-retention-tagged endpoint by OpenRouter, none tagged EU
classes.C: no zero-retention-tagged endpoint: only the lab's own host, under the lab's own terms
classes.D: Anthropic Covered Model: kept at least 30 days by default on every surface; a limited-time zero-retention option exists for eligible customers, for their own internal business applications, whom Anthropic or their cloud provider contacts or who request consideration, and OpenRouter tags no such endpoint

openrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol.labRetention: abuse-monitoring logs up to 30 days; Responses API application state 30 days by default
openrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol.labTraining: not used to train by default
openrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol.wording: GPT-6.1 Sol via OpenRouter, routed only to endpoints OpenRouter tags zero-data-retention (Azure, one of them EU). That is OpenRouter's record. Microsoft's abuse monitoring reviews prompts automatically and stores nothing for that; if that is not enough, a prompt can be stored for a person to read, unless modified abuse monitoring is approved. Whether OpenRouter's Azure account has that approval is not stated.

openrouter/openai/gpt-6-astra.labTraining: not used to train by default
openrouter/openai/gpt-6-astra.wording: GPT-6 Astra via OpenRouter, routed only to endpoints OpenRouter tags zero-data-retention (Azure, US or unsuffixed; none is tagged EU). That is OpenRouter's record. Microsoft's abuse monitoring reviews prompts automatically and stores nothing for that; if that is not enough, a prompt can be stored for a person to read, unless modified abuse monitoring is approved. openrouter/google/gemini-3.8-flash.labRetention: 55 days of logging for the Gemini API (AI Studio) per Google's abuse-monitoring page; on Vertex, flagged prompts are stored up to 90 days, and Google Cloud Master Agreement customers are exempt by default
openrouter/google/gemini-3.8-flash.labTraining: paid tier: not used to improve Google products; free tier: used, human review possible
openrouter/google/gemini-3.8-flash.wording: Gemini 3.8 Flash via OpenRouter, routed to Vertex endpoints OpenRouter tags zero-data-retention (global and US regions, no EU tag; the US one costs more than the shipped price limit of $0.75 in / $3.75 out per million tokens, so a seat at that limit does not reach it). Google's Vertex page says flagged prompts may be logged for abuse monitoring and stored for up to 90 days, and that customers under a Google Cloud Master Agreement are exempt from that logging by default (whether OpenRouter's Google Cloud account is under such an agreement is not stated); the Gemini API page, a different service, says Google keeps prompts, context and outputs for 55 days for abuse detection.

openrouter/meta/muse-spark-1.3.wording: Muse Spark 1.3 via OpenRouter, sent to Meta's own API (no zero-data-retention endpoint exists). Meta's docs say Standard-tier data is not used for training; they state no retention period or region.
